title: What the Discovery Laboratory is
description: The laboratory automates the experimental side of mathematics: compute many examples, detect patterns, formulate conjectures, search for proofs, and verify with proof assistants where possible. It produces conjectures with evidence and proofs with certificates — and labels everything honestly by verification rung.

title: Pattern detection algorithm
description: Given computed examples, the detector finds patterns: closed forms via symbolic regression, recurrences via sequence analysis, divisibility and modular patterns via number-theoretic scans. Candidate patterns are ranked by simplicity and fit — the simplest pattern fitting all examples wins the conjecture slot.

title: Reasoning: proof search and verification
description: Proof search tries tactics, lemma combinations, and induction schemes against the formal statement; successes become certificates checked by the proof assistant's kernel. title: Failure modes: false patterns and rung fraud
description: The laboratory fails by finding patterns in noise (overfitting small examples) or by claiming rungs without evidence. Defenses: minimum example counts per claim type, holdout validation of patterns, and kernel-level verification for the top rung. A 'proved' claim without a certificate is rejected by the schema.
